title: Reliability and Resource Management
subtopics: Avoiding unbounded loops and result sets
learning_outcomes: Explain the role of reliability and resource management in a Classic ASP application.
Identify and describe at least two syllabus subtopics: Closing database connections and Releasing ADO objects.
Inspect a minimal example and define a reproducible normal-case and failure-case test.

content.intro: In this lesson, you will study reliability and resource management as part of Classic ASP development and legacy maintenance. The lesson follows the attached ASP curriculum topic 105 and uses the syllabus subtopics as the coverage checklist.
content.why_it_matters: Reliability and Resource Management matters because Classic ASP behavior crosses a server-side scripting engine, IIS configuration, request/response boundaries, and often COM or ADO dependencies. A small, explicit test helps distinguish intended behavior from runtime-specific behavior.

content_blocks.title: The core idea
content_blocks.text: Production readiness means controlled configuration, limited privileges, measured performance, resource cleanup, repeatable deployment, and recoverable backups. For 'Reliability and Resource Management', record the exact IIS and OS assumptions, test the plan in a non-production environment, and define verification plus rollback criteria before changing live settings.

content_blocks.title: Syllabus coverage
content_blocks.text: The lesson explicitly covers: Closing database connections; Releasing ADO objects; Handling external service failures; Timeouts and retries; Avoiding unbounded loops and result sets; Logging and monitoring; Recovery after application restarts. Treat these subtopics as connected requirements. For each one, be able to define the concept, identify where it appears in a Classic ASP application, and name one test or diagnostic that would verify it.

content_blocks.title: Inspectable example: Reliability and Resource Management
content_blocks.code:
<%
If IsObject(rs) Then
  If rs.State <> 0 Then rs.Close
  Set rs = Nothing
End If
If IsObject(conn) Then
  If conn.State <> 0 Then conn.Close
  Set conn = Nothing
End If
%>
content_blocks.expected_output: Open ADO objects are closed where applicable and object references are released.
content_blocks.run_instructions: Production cleanup must account for errors during cleanup and objects that were never successfully initialized; record the primary failure separately. The standard CodeLeaf browser playground previews HTML/CSS/JavaScript only; it does not execute Classic ASP, VBScript, ADO, IIS commands, PowerShell, or SQL. This block is therefore marked for static inspection unless you run it in the clearly identified local tool.
content_blocks.reset_steps: Restore the original sample and test data. Change one condition, input, provider setting, or runtime option at a time, then compare observed behavior with the expected result.
content_blocks.limitations: Not executed during course generation. Classic ASP examples require a configured Windows/IIS environment with the matching ASP scripting engine and any required COM/ADO providers. Provider-specific and IIS-version-specific behavior must be verified locally.

content_blocks.title: Runtime and safety checkpoint
content_blocks.text: Use a staging environment, written acceptance criteria, version-controlled changes, and a rollback plan. Record evidence instead of claiming a deployment or migration was tested if it was not. The source syllabus treats Classic ASP as a legacy maintenance technology, not as ASP.NET or a default choice for new web projects.

content_blocks.title: Guided workflow
content_blocks.text: 1. Start with a minimal local example of reliability and resource management. 2. Trace its inputs, state changes, dependencies, and output. 3. Test a normal case, a missing/malformed case, and one permission/provider/runtime failure. 4. Write down the exact expected and observed result before changing another variable.

content_blocks.title: Try it yourself
content_blocks.text: Create a small, reviewable demonstration of reliability and resource management using synthetic data. Include at least one of these syllabus concepts: Closing database connections. State the expected result first, then add one invalid or boundary case and explain how your program should behave.

common_mistakes.problem: Treating legacy runtime behavior as universal.
common_mistakes.why: IIS versions, Windows lifecycle, COM registration/bitness, and ADO providers can change behavior.
common_mistakes.fix: Write down the actual server/provider versions and validate on a disposable test site.

common_mistakes.why: Empty input, missing records, expired sessions, permissions, timeouts, and malformed data reveal different failure modes.
common_mistakes.fix: Add normal, negative, and boundary cases with expected outcomes.

common_mistakes.why: Detailed errors can reveal paths, SQL text, configuration, and component information.
common_mistakes.fix: Keep diagnostics in restricted server-side logs and return a generic message with a reference ID.

summary: Reliability and Resource Management is one step in the larger Classic ASP request, state, data, security, or maintenance workflow.

The syllabus coverage includes Closing database connections; Releasing ADO objects; Handling external service failures; Timeouts and retries; Avoiding unbounded loops and result sets; Logging and monitoring; Recovery after application restarts.
A reproducible legacy-code example records input, environment/version, expected outcome, observed outcome, and a meaningful failure case.
expected_output: Open ADO objects are closed where applicable and object references are released.

common_mistakes.problem: Assuming syntax alone proves the application works.
common_mistakes.why: IIS configuration, permissions, COM activation, database providers, and response behavior are external dependencies.
common_mistakes.fix: Run against the documented local test host and record exact evidence.

common_mistakes.why: Query strings, form fields, cookies, and hidden controls remain client-controlled.
common_mistakes.fix: Validate on the server and apply authorization and output encoding at the appropriate boundary.
